body:
CHIEF: I SAID THE ORDERING QUESTION WAS A ONE-LINE MEASUREMENT AND I OWED YOU THE ANSWER RATHER THAN
THE CAVEAT. Ran it. The answer is "deterministic, but by accident", which is worse than either
branch I offered you.

MEASURED, executing the same shape as candidates.scala:127:

  Ordering[Double] in scope   scala.math.Ordering$DeprecatedDoubleOrdering$
  compare(NaN, 1.0)           1        NaN is GREATER than every real number
  compare(NaN, NaN)           0        so it IS a total order
  sortBy on (0.5, NaN, 0.1)   0.1, 0.5, NaN

SO YOUR "EXPLICIT DETERMINISTIC ORDERING" REQUIREMENT IS CURRENTLY SATISFIED BY A DEPRECATED
IMPLICIT. Determinism is not declared anywhere; it is inherited from
`Ordering$DeprecatedDoubleOrdering`, which Scala 2.13 introduced precisely because the total-vs-IEEE
choice was too important to leave implicit. The moment that deprecation is enforced, or someone
imports IeeeOrdering for a good local reason, the nomination order becomes non-total and this code
changes behaviour with no diff at the call site. Declaring the ordering is therefore part of your
design, not a cleanup after it.

AND THE CONSEQUENCE AT THE TAKE IS NOT WHAT I EXPECTED:

  :127  .sortBy { case (r, d) => (d, r.key) }     NaN sorts LAST
  :128  .take(perLevel)

A node whose provider returns NaN is silently sorted BELOW every real candidate and then DROPPED by
the take. It is not detected, not recorded, and not reported as malformed - it simply stops being a
candidate. That is fail-closed on the ordering and SILENT on the science: the audit trail you are
designing would show that node was never nominated, with no indication that a provider returned a
non-finite distance for it.

BUT IT ONLY HOLDS WHILE THERE ARE MORE SCORED NODES THAN perLevel. If a level scores fewer nodes
than the take width, the NaN entry SURVIVES and `Some(NaN)` enters Nomination.rawScore and the
published record. So the current safety is a function of how many nodes happen to score at that
level - which is data-dependent, not structural.

WHICH SHARPENS MY EARLIER POINT RATHER THAN WITHDRAWING IT: your "finite raw score" requirement still
belongs at :124, before the sort. Not because ordering breaks - it does not today - but because the
two failure modes below it are SILENT NODE LOSS and NaN REACHING THE RECORD, and which one you get
depends on the corpus.

I have not changed any code. This closes the question I raised; the design decision is yours.
